questions.question: Sami asks Mina: 'What is the key to periodontal diagnosis?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Periodontal diagnosis is based on probing and X-rays.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will always do both.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How to evaluate periodontal bone loss?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'X-rays are essential to evaluate bone loss.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will always prescribe X-rays.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is bleeding on probing (BOP)?' Mina replies:
options: A sign of poor hygiene only
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'BOP is an indicator of active inflammation.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will always note the BOP.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What are the risk factors for periodontitis?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Risk factors are multiple and must be taken into account.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will look for these factors systematically.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'How is a periodontal pocket defined?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'A pocket is defined by probing > 3 mm.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will measure systematically.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is the Miller classification?' Mina explains:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Miller classifies recessions according to the coverage prognosis.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will use this classification.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What are the clinical signs of gingivitis?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Gingivitis manifests as inflammation of the soft tissues.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will identify these signs.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is the difference between gingivitis and periodontitis?' Mina replies:
options: Gingivitis is reversible, periodontitis has bone loss
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Gingivitis is reversible, periodontitis involves bone loss.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will differentiate the two.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What are the advantages of non-surgical periodontal treatment?' Mina replies:
options: Less invasive, effective on pockets < 5 mm
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Non-surgical treatment is the first step for shallow pockets.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will start with non-surgical.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'When should a periodontal flap be performed?' Mina replies:
options: For pockets > 5 mm with bone loss
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The flap is indicated for access to deep pockets.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will refer to a specialist.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is periodontal maintenance?' Mina replies:
options: Regular follow-up after treatment to prevent relapses
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Maintenance is essential for long-term stability.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will plan regular check-ups.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What are the prognostic factors in periodontology?' Mina replies:
options: Pocket depth, bone loss, mobility, furcations
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Prognosis is multifactorial.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will evaluate all these parameters.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is guided tissue regeneration?' Mina replies:
options: A technique using membranes to regenerate bone
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'GTR allows regeneration of lost bone.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will train in GTR.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How to manage a Grade 2 furcation?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Furcations require an adapted approach.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will treat furcations with care.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What are the signs of active periodontitis?' Mina replies:
options: Bleeding on probing, suppuration, progressive bone loss
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Disease activity is multifactorial.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will monitor these signs.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'When to use antibiotics in periodontology?' Mina replies:
options: In aggressive periodontitis or when scaling is insufficient
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Antibiotics are indicated in specific cases.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will prescribe them sparingly.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is Grade 2 tooth mobility?' Mina replies:
options: Horizontal mobility of less than 1 mm
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Grade 2 mobility corresponds to displacement of 1-2 mm.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will use this classification.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is the impact of diabetes on the periodontium?' Mina replies:
options: Diabetes increases the risk and severity of periodontitis
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Diabetes is a major risk factor.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will always ask about diabetic status.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What are the objectives of periodontal treatment?' Mina replies:
options: Eliminate inflammation, reduce pockets, preserve dentition
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The objectives are multiple and complementary.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will aim for all these objectives.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is a Miller Class I gingival recession?' Mina replies:
options: A recession with complete coverage possible
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Miller I has a good coverage prognosis.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will propose a graft for this recession.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'Why is periodontal maintenance important?' Mina replies:
options: To prevent relapses and maintain stability
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Maintenance is the key to long-term stability.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will plan regular maintenance.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How to manage a smoking patient in periodontology?' Mina replies:
options: Inform about risks and encourage smoking cessation
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Smoking cessation improves treatment results.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will encourage smoking cessation.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What are the signs of aggressive periodontitis?' Mina replies:
options: Rapid bone loss in young and healthy patients
Slow bone loss in elderly patients
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Aggressive periodontitis occurs in young patients.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will screen for these cases.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is the place of lasers in periodontology?' Mina replies:
options: A complementary tool, but not a replacement for scaling
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The laser is complementary, not a substitute.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will use the laser as a complement.'

questions.question: Sami, after having mastered periodontal diagnosis with Mina, says: 'I am ready to take on all challenges!' Mina concludes: 'Mastering periodontal diagnosis is...'
options: The basis of success in periodontology
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Mastering periodontal diagnosis is the basis of success in periodontology.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will continue to train.'
